claims.text: Ola reportedly receives about 80,000 service complaints per month (Sept 2024).
claims.quote: Insiders familiar with the matter revealed that the Bengaluru-based company receives an average of 80,000 service complaints per month, overwhelming its existing service centers.

passage.text: • Manufacturing News Ola Electric Creates Team to Address 80K Monthly Service Issues • MM Desk • 19/09/2024 Image Courtesy: Ola Electric Ola Electric, the manufacturer of battery-powered scooters, has assembled a new service team to address an escalating wave of customer complaints concerning service-related issues. Insiders familiar with the matter revealed that the Bengaluru-based company receives an average of 80,000 service complaints per month, overwhelming its existing service centers.

passage.text: That’s something those new to EVs will like. Eco mode caps the speed to 50kph, which is the typical pace in most cities, while Power mode allows you to hit an indicated 80kph. The ability to hold these speeds means the iQube doesn’t feel out of place on a faster flowing highway as well. What will take some getting used to on the iQube is its aggressive motor regen when you shut the throttle. We think it’s a little too strong and doesn’t feel very natural, although this is something the company can address in a software update.

recommendation.headline: TVS iQube, tentatively, mainly because the evidence argues against Ola on your top priority
recommendation.summary: Evidence on reliability and service for Ather, TVS and Bajaj is thin; Ola's service problems are well documented, so a established-maker scooter such as the iQube is the safer pick pending test rides.

reasons.text: Ola has documented service problems (80,000 complaints a month, 30-45 day waits).
iQube Power mode reaches indicated 80kph and the scooter has good ergonomics.
Bigger-battery iQube variants offer decent range for daily use.

tradeoffs.text: Aggressive regen and no verified Bengaluru service data for TVS.
